about: Agent Watch plain-English explanations. First matching rule wins, so put specific rules above general ones. Match fields (all optional, case-insensitive .NET regex): name = exe name, path = full exe path, cmd = command line, parent = parent exe name. risk: green = normal helper, yellow = can act for you / network / MCP tool server, screen = screen-control helper (Yellow while loaded and idle, Red when active). category: agent / mcp / screen-control / model-server / service (which ones show is set by showCategories; 'Show model servers' in the app adds model-server). agent: true makes a matching process show as its own app in the summary. Agent Watch reloads this file automatically when it changes.

rules.name: ^antigravity\.exe$
rules.what: An OpenBot AI agent powered by Google Gemini through the Antigravity runtime. It can run commands and start its own screen driver.
rules.why: An OpenBot chat or task is using the Gemini agent.
rules.todo: Normal while that OpenBot task runs. Stop the task in OpenBot to end it.

rules.name: ^pi\.exe$
rules.what: An OpenBot AI agent powered by DeepSeek through the Pi runtime. It can run commands and start its own screen driver.
rules.why: An OpenBot chat or task is using the DeepSeek agent.
rules.todo: Normal while that OpenBot task runs. Stop the task in OpenBot to end it.

rules.name: ^grok\.exe$
rules.what: An OpenBot AI agent powered by Grok.
rules.why: An OpenBot chat or task is using the Grok agent.
rules.todo: Normal while that OpenBot task runs.

rules.name: ^codex\.exe$
rules.what: An OpenBot AI agent powered by OpenAI Codex.
rules.why: An OpenBot chat or task is using the Codex agent.
rules.todo: Normal while that OpenBot task runs.

rules.what: An AI provider runtime that OpenBot downloaded and runs for one of its agents.
rules.why: An OpenBot chat or task is using that provider.
rules.todo: Normal while that OpenBot task runs.

rules.name: ^chatgpt\.exe$
rules.what: OpenAI's Codex coding app. It shows up as ChatGPT.exe because it is built on the ChatGPT desktop shell. The many ChatGPT.exe copies are its window, graphics and tab helpers (normal for Electron apps).
rules.why: You opened Codex (or it started with Windows).
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore. Closing Codex stops this and everything under it.

rules.name: ^chatgpt\.exe$
rules.what: OpenAI's ChatGPT desktop app and its window helpers.
rules.why: You opened ChatGPT (or it started with Windows).
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore. Close ChatGPT to stop it.

rules.name: ^codex-computer-use
rules.what: Lets Codex take screenshots of your desktop and move the mouse or type when a Codex task uses Computer Use.
rules.why: Codex loads it at startup so it is ready. It only acts when a Codex task is using Computer Use.
rules.todo: Idle (Yellow) is fine. If it turns Red when you did not ask Codex to use your screen, stop the Codex task or close Codex. You can turn Computer Use off in Codex settings.

rules.name: ^node\.exe$
rules.what: The Codex plugin that drives Computer Use (screenshots, clicks, typing). Runs on Codex's bundled Node.js.
rules.why: Started by the Codex agent engine so Computer Use is available to tasks.
rules.todo: Idle (Yellow) is fine. If it turns Red unexpectedly, stop the Codex task or close Codex.

rules.name: ^node_repl\.exe$
rules.what: A small JavaScript sandbox Codex uses to run tool code (part of its bundled Node.js runtime).
rules.why: Started by the Codex agent engine or its computer-use plugin.
rules.todo: Normal while Codex is open. Close Codex to stop it.

rules.what: A Codex plugin that gives Codex security-review tools over MCP (Model Context Protocol).
rules.why: The Codex Security plugin is installed and enabled.
rules.todo: Normal. Disable the plugin in Codex if you don't use it.

rules.what: Built-in Codex tools (app actions) served to the Codex agent over MCP.
rules.why: Part of the Codex app; starts with it.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.what: A Codex plugin that gives Codex data-analysis tools over MCP.
rules.why: The Data Analytics plugin is installed and enabled in Codex.
rules.todo: Normal. Disable the plugin in Codex if you don't use it.

rules.what: A Codex plugin running on Codex's bundled Node.js (the folder is called cua_node, but most of these are ordinary tool servers, not screen control).
rules.why: Started by the Codex agent engine for an enabled plugin.
rules.todo: Normal while Codex is open.

rules.what: Codex's background Node.js runtime that powers parts of the app.
rules.why: Starts with the Codex app.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^codex\.exe$
rules.what: The Codex agent itself. It reads and edits files and runs commands for you, and starts Codex's tool servers (MCP).
rules.why: Runs whenever the Codex app is open.
rules.todo: Normal while Codex is open. Close Codex to stop it.

rules.name: ^codex\.exe$
rules.what: Connects this PC to Codex cloud so cloud tasks can run commands here. It uses the network.
rules.why: Codex started it for remote or cloud task support.
rules.todo: Normal if you use Codex cloud tasks. Close Codex to stop it.

rules.name: ^codex\.exe$
rules.what: The Codex command-line agent. It can read and edit files and run commands.
rules.why: Codex or a terminal started it.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using Codex.

rules.name: ^codex-windows-sandbox
rules.what: A Windows service Codex uses to run commands in a locked-down sandbox.
rules.why: Installed with Codex; runs as a service.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^codex-code-mode-host
rules.what: Runs the scripts Codex writes when it works in 'code mode'.
rules.why: Started by the Codex agent engine.
rules.todo: Normal while Codex is open.

rules.name: ^gk(-alpha)?\.exe$
rules.what: GitKraken's MCP server. It gives an AI agent git and GitHub tools (status, commits, branches, pull requests).
rules.why: An agent (Codex or Claude) is set up to use the GitKraken MCP plugin.
rules.todo: Normal if you want agents to use git. Remove the GitKraken MCP plugin from that agent to stop it.

rules.what: Launches GitKraken's MCP server through npx so an agent can use git tools.
rules.why: An agent is set up to use the GitKraken MCP plugin.
rules.todo: Normal if you want agents to use git.

rules.what: An MCP tool server from the rea-agents npm package that the agent can call.
rules.why: It is configured as an MCP server for this agent.
rules.todo: Normal if you added it on purpose.

rules.what: An MCP server that lets the agent read PDF files.
rules.why: Configured as an MCP server for this agent.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^openbot\.exe$
rules.what: The OpenBot app and its window helpers. OpenBot runs several AI agents (Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, Codex) that can use your computer.
rules.why: You opened OpenBot (or it started with Windows).
rules.todo: Close OpenBot to stop it and all of its agents. Turn off Computer Use in OpenBot settings if you don't want it touching your screen.

rules.name: ^cua-driver\.exe$
rules.what: OpenBot's screen-control driver. It lists your open windows, takes screenshots and can click and type. The 'serve' copy is OpenBot's main one; 'mcp' copies belong to one of its agents. It writes cua-driver.log while it scans windows.
rules.why: OpenBot starts one at launch, and each OpenBot agent that may use the screen starts its own.
rules.todo: Idle (Yellow) is fine. If it turns Red and you did not ask OpenBot to use your screen, stop the OpenBot chat or close OpenBot, or turn off Computer Use in OpenBot settings.

rules.name: ^cursor\.exe$
rules.what: Cursor, the AI code editor. Its agent can edit files and run terminal commands in your projects.
rules.why: You opened Cursor.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using it. Close Cursor to stop it.

rules.name: ^windsurf\.exe$
rules.what: Windsurf, an AI code editor whose agent can edit files and run commands.
rules.why: You opened Windsurf.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using it.

rules.name: ^antigravity\.exe$
rules.what: Google's Antigravity agent IDE (Gemini). Its agents can edit files, run commands and use a browser.
rules.why: You opened Antigravity.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using it.

rules.what: Google's Gemini command-line agent. It can read and edit files and run commands.
rules.why: Someone started gemini in a terminal.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using it. Exit it in its terminal.

rules.what: Google's Gemini desktop app.
rules.why: Starts with Windows (Run key).
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^aider
rules.what: Aider, a command-line AI coding agent that edits files and makes git commits.
rules.why: Someone started aider in a terminal.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using it.

rules.name: ^python
rules.what: Aider, a command-line AI coding agent that edits files and makes git commits.
rules.why: Someone started aider in a terminal.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using it.

rules.name: ^github\.exe$
rules.what: The GitHub Copilot desktop app; its agent can work on your repositories.
rules.why: Starts with Windows (Run key).
rules.todo: Normal if you use it.

rules.name: ^warp\.exe$
rules.what: Warp terminal. Its built-in AI agent can run commands for you.
rules.why: Starts with Windows (Run key).
rules.todo: Normal if you use it.

rules.name: ^llama-(server|cli)\.exe$
rules.what: A llama.cpp local model server.
rules.why: You or a script started it.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^blender\.exe$
rules.what: Blender, the 3D modelling and rendering app.
rules.why: Started by you, or by an agent task (look at the parent: an OpenBot agent starts it for 3D work).
rules.todo: If an agent started it for a task you didn't ask for, stop that task.

rules.name: ^claude\.exe$
rules.what: Anthropic's Claude desktop app and its window helpers.
rules.why: You opened Claude (or it started with Windows).
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore. Close Claude to stop it and its tool servers.

rules.name: ^claude\.exe$
rules.what: Anthropic's Claude Code command-line agent. It can read and edit files and run commands in its terminal.
rules.why: Someone started claude in a terminal.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using Claude Code. Exit it in its terminal to stop it.

rules.name: ^node\.exe$
rules.what: Anthropic's Claude Code agent running on Node.js. It can read and edit files and run commands.
rules.why: Someone started claude in a terminal.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using Claude Code.

rules.name: ^grok bot\.exe$
rules.what: The Grok Bot desktop app. It lets Grok Bot run PowerShell commands on this PC for your requests; those show as powershell.exe under it.
rules.why: You opened Grok Bot (or it started with Windows).
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore. Close Grok Bot to stop it.

rules.name: ^(powershell|pwsh|bash|wsl)\.exe$
rules.what: A shell (PowerShell, bash or WSL) that an AI agent opened to run commands on your PC.
rules.why: The agent above it is carrying out a task.
rules.todo: Normal during a task. If you didn't ask for anything, check that agent's chat.

rules.name: ^opencode\.exe$
rules.what: The OpenCode coding agent server. It can edit files and run commands, and talks to LM Studio for its model.
rules.why: Started at logon so OpenCode is always available.
rules.todo: Normal - this is your own setup.

rules.name: ^opencodex?-desktop\.exe$
rules.what: The OpenCode desktop window.
rules.why: You opened OpenCode (or it started with Windows).
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^ollama app\.exe$
rules.what: Ollama's tray icon and launcher.
rules.why: Starts with Windows (Startup folder).
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^ollama.*\.exe$
rules.what: Runs local AI models and serves them on this PC (port 11434).
rules.why: Started by the Ollama tray app.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore. Quit Ollama from its tray icon to free GPU memory.

rules.name: ^(lm studio|lms|llmster.*)\.exe$
rules.what: LM Studio, your local model server used by OpenCode.
rules.why: Starts with Windows as a service (--run-as-service).
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.what: Strata's terminal agent (Python). It can run commands on this PC.
rules.why: You opened Strata.
rules.todo: Normal if you are using Strata. Close Strata to stop it.

rules.name: ^invokeai
rules.what: InvokeAI's local web server for AI image generation.
rules.why: Started from a Command Prompt (invokeai-web).
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore. Close its window to free GPU memory.

rules.name: ^python
rules.what: The Python process that does InvokeAI's image work.
rules.why: Started by InvokeAI.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^cloudflared\.exe$
rules.what: Your Cloudflare tunnel. It makes local services (for example OpenCode) reachable from the internet.
rules.why: Started by its scheduled task at logon.
rules.todo: Normal - this is your own setup. Stopping it cuts remote access to those services.

rules.name: ^docker-agent\.exe$
rules.what: Docker Desktop's AI assistant/agent plugin.
rules.why: Started by Docker Desktop.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^(docker desktop|com\.docker\..*)\.exe$
rules.what: Docker Desktop and its background engine. It also starts WSL.
rules.why: Starts with Windows.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^msrdc\.exe$
rules.what: Shows Linux app windows from WSL on your desktop. It uses the Remote Desktop client internally, but only inside this PC - nobody is remoting in.
rules.why: WSL started (Docker Desktop starts it automatically).
rules.todo: Harmless - safe to ignore. It goes away when WSL shuts down.

rules.name: ^(msrdc|mstsc)\.exe$
rules.what: A Remote Desktop client session (outside WSL).
rules.why: Someone opened a Remote Desktop connection.
rules.todo: If you didn't open it, close it and check Remote Desktop settings.

rules.name: ^(anydesk|teamviewer.*|rustdesk|winvnc.*|tvnserver|vncserver.*|uvnc_service|parsecd|remoting_host|screenconnect.*)\.exe$
rules.what: A remote-access app that can show and control your screen from another device.
rules.why: It is installed and running.
rules.todo: If you didn't install it or aren't using it, quit it.

rules.name: ^(autohotkey.*|nircmd.*)\.exe$
rules.what: An automation tool that can send keystrokes and mouse clicks.
rules.why: A script or app started it.
rules.todo: If you don't recognise the script, quit it from its tray icon.

rules.name: ^python
rules.what: A Python script using screen-automation tools (pyautogui / computer use).
rules.why: An agent or script started it.
rules.todo: If you didn't start it, check its parent app.

rules.what: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool server. It gives an AI agent extra abilities, like reading files or calling a web service.
rules.why: The agent above it has this MCP server configured.
rules.todo: Normal if you set it up. Remove it from that agent's MCP settings to stop it.

rules.name: ^cmd\.exe$
rules.what: A hidden Command Prompt used to start another program (often an MCP tool server).
rules.why: The app above it used it as a launcher.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: ^conhost\.exe$
rules.what: Windows' console helper that every command-line program gets.
rules.why: Created automatically by Windows.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.

rules.name: crashpad|crash_?handler|crashreporter
rules.what: Collects a crash report if the app crashes.
rules.why: Starts with the app.
rules.todo: Normal - safe to ignore.
